verdicts.reason: Both put the 'Taste the Glow' CTA at the very top, above the product and headline, so the reading order is reversed. In both, the can floats off-centre from its backing circle and the bottom third is dead space. B is slightly worse: its headline runs almost to both canvas edges (about 25px margins) and the CTA is jammed into the top-left corner.

A stacks the CTA above the headline (wrong order), the subtitle sits on the decorative circle, the can is detached from its circle and the bottom is empty. B shrinks the CTA to an illegibly tiny pill dropped arbitrarily in the bottom-left, off any grid, which buries the action. Its headline also nearly touches the right edge.

The two are nearly identical. Both have a tiny, near-illegible CTA stranded in the bottom-left, not aligned to the text column, with a big empty band between the can and the button. A's headline crowds both canvas edges and its CTA's left edge doesn't line up with the text. B keeps better side margins and its CTA aligns to the text column.

A has the tiny, buried CTA in the bottom-left, off-grid, with a large dead zone above it. B keeps the CTA at a readable size but puts it above the headline (wrong order), its headline crowds both edges, the copy overlaps the circle, and the bottom quarter is empty.
